lean.statement:
∀ {E : Type u_1}
  [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace E] {f : E → ℝ},
  ContDiff ℝ 2 f →
    ∀ (x v : E),
      inner ℝ (gradient f (x + v) - gradient f x) v = ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..1, ((fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (x + t • v)) v) v
approved_definition_context: ContDiff ℝ 2 f means that the real Frechet derivative exists everywhere and is continuously Frechet differentiable.
For a complete real inner-product space, gradient f x is the Riesz vector of fderiv ℝ f x, so inner ℝ (gradient f x) v = fderiv ℝ f x v.
The expression (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x v) v is the second Frechet derivative evaluated twice at v. Under the displayed regularity it is a genuine second derivative.
The notation ∫ t in 0..1 denotes the oriented real interval integral with respect to Lebesgue measure.
StrongConvexOn Set.univ m f means: for all x,y and a,b>=0 with a+b=1, f(a • x+b • y)<=a*f(x)+b*f(y)-a*b*(m/2*norm(x-y)^2). The definition itself does not restrict the sign of m.
EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is real d-dimensional Euclidean space, including d=0.
